title: Elevation Certificates and Re-Rating Under NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
### Elevation Certificate guidance — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)

Under Risk Rating 2.0 an Elevation Certificate is optional (the tier setting is that a certificate is not required for rating); the rating engine otherwise uses its own estimated first floor height.

**Acceptance.** A certificate is accepted only on FEMA Form 086-0-33, completed and sealed by a licensed land surveyor, engineer or architect, for the building as it currently stands.

**Re-rating.** When the tier uses the certified first floor height, the first floor height certified on an accepted certificate is submitted to the rating engine and the engine returns the full-term risk premium and ICC premium with that height.

**Applying the certificate.** The certificate is applied only when the re-rated full-term risk premium plus ICC premium is lower than the rated figures on the policy; otherwise it is kept on file as not applied and the rating is not changed. A certificate is applied only on a policy whose status is pending effective or in force, as shown on Tidemark's policy record.

**The re-rate credit.** An applied certificate takes effect on the date it is received, and the reduction is credited as re-rate components: the risk premium credit is the fall in the full-term risk premium and the ICC premium credit is the fall in the full-term ICC premium, each multiplied by the days from the receipt date to the term end divided by the days from the term start to the term end and rounded to the cent, and the Reserve Fund Assessment credit is the tier's Reserve Fund Assessment percentage of those two pro rata credits, rounded to the cent. The HFIAA surcharge and the Federal Policy Fee are not affected.

*Clause no longer in force:* "The credit is refunded to the payor of record." This clause is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis.

**Next renewal.** From the next renewal the re-rated premium is the prior-term figure the annual cap is measured from.

| Accepted certificate, re-rated risk plus ICC premium compared with the rated figures | Policy status | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Lower | Pending effective or in force | Applied; re-rate credits from the receipt date |
| Equal or higher | Any | Kept on file, not applied; rating unchanged |
| Lower | Renewal grace, lapsed, cancelled or nullified | Not applied |

*Hypothetical worked example.* On a 365-day term, a certificate received with 146 days left lowers a hypothetical full-term risk premium by 500.00 dollars and the ICC premium by 0.00. The risk premium credit is 500.00 multiplied by 146 and divided by 365, that is 200.00; at a hypothetical 18 percent the Reserve Fund Assessment credit is 36.00.

superseded_clauses: The credit is refunded to the payor of record.
